purpose: Questions that future sources should answer automatically when possible before asking the user.

questions.question: Which portions of the 2018 driver hiring/orientation/training workflow remain current, and what newer forms or systems supersede its paper workflow?
Is the March 2023 employee handbook the current handbook? If not, locate the superseding version and effective date.
questions.resolution_note: Resolved from the supplied December 15, 2025 Employee Handbook, which is the newer full handbook source currently modeled. The March 2023 selected handbook/discipline record is historical and has been linked as superseded.

questions.question: What exact date and organizational change led from the early-2026 HR & EEO Manager assignment to the EEO Manager/Officer named in the 2026-08-26 signed statement?
Are the 2023 Group A-D disciplinary guidelines still current, and what present-day HR review/approval steps govern discipline?
questions.resolution_note: The December 15, 2025 handbook supersedes the 2023 Group A-D guidelines for current use and preserves current progressive-discipline language. The remaining open portion is the present-day corrective-action form, HR review/approval chain, and investigation/documentation standard.

questions.question: Document RTEC's complete current workplace injury/workers' compensation/OSHA workflow on top of the now-validated Kentucky baseline: current insurer/claims administrator, carrier intake method, internal owners/backups, incident form, emergency/safety escalation, Kentucky OSH reporter, medical-record separation, lost-time/light-duty/RTW, OSHA log reconciliation, closure and retention.
questions.resolution_note: Current Kentucky baseline is now validated: employer reports work-related/alleged work-related injury or disease to its carrier/benefits administrator within three working days; carrier/administrator handles required FROI to DWC for qualifying lost-time cases; Kentucky OSH currently requires covered fatalities within 8 hours and hospitalization/amputation/loss-of-eye within 24 hours. RTEC-specific carrier, portal, forms, ownership and closure workflow remain unresolved.

questions.question: Document the complete current vehicle-accident workflow, including notification, internal forms, police/insurance reporting, preventability review, training, discipline and closure.
questions.resolution_note: Historical/current evidence now establishes several components: unsafe/out-of-service vehicles must not continue in service until cleared; vehicle incidents were historically tracked in the fiscal event register; accident cases may use police/DOT and video evidence; current video policy imposes accident-recording retention; historical training allowed corrective defensive-driving retraining. Current first-notification, preventability, insurance/state/federal reporting, clearance authority and case-closure steps remain unresolved.

questions.question: Locate the current RTEC 401-K Summary Plan Description/plan booklet and recordkeeper, then document the current eligibility/entry rules, enrollment/change method, HR-finance-payroll ownership, remittance/feed, notices and retention. Resolve the public website's 'after 30 days' claim against that governing plan document.
questions.resolution_note: Current handbook confirms a 401-K Employee Savings Plan with pretax payroll deduction and employer match for full-time active employees but explicitly defers detailed service/eligibility requirements to the plan booklet. The current RTEC public job board advertises 401-K eligibility after 30 days. Public Form-5500-derived history corroborates RTEC 401(K) PLAN, plan 001, through a filing period dated 2024-07-01, while historical public data associates Hartford only with a 2014 filing. Targeted Drive, Library, GitHub, connected-Outlook and public-authority searches still did not surface the current SPD/plan booklet or current recordkeeper. Therefore current plan existence is corroborated but the public 30-day rule, current recordkeeper and operative enrollment/feed workflow remain unvalidated.

Identify the process/script and approved wording behind the 2026 Rejection Emails workbook and the human-review/send steps.
questions.resolution_note: The current canonical workflow is in unwit1/job-applicant-dashboard. Remaining work is to reconcile the exact approved wording/version of each live template and any 2026 Rejection Emails workbook against the canonical template files.

FTA withdrew Circular 4704.1A effective 2026-06-05 and says the withdrawal eliminates the Circular-based EEO Program plan/document submission and FTA review burden while preserving underlying nondiscrimination obligations. KYTC's current transit resources still require EEO compliance, but the latest located State Management Plan (2024) still contains pre-withdrawal Circular language; current Kentucky pass-through documentation expectations remain unresolved.

questions.resolution_note: FTA withdrew Circular 4704.1A in June 2026, so historical utilization/goals methodology is no longer presumed to be part of a current federal recurring submission. Methodology remains important for historical auditability and may still matter if KYTC/OTD requires a current state/pass-through program.

Determine whether RTEC currently has a covered Kentucky state procurement/contract event or contracting-agency request that requires a new EEO Contract Compliance approval after the current approval expires September 30, 2026. If triggered, capture the agency request, electronic submission/packet, approval date, new expiration date and current owner.
questions.resolution_note: Current Kentucky Finance guidance says apparent low bidders provide EEO information through the contracting agency and approved vendors receive one-year approval. Current KYTC response instructions say Finance does not pre-approve vendors and unsolicited submissions are not processed. Therefore the 2026-09-30 expiration should not by itself generate an unsolicited annual filing task. Internal evidence still does not show a successor approval or whether RTEC currently has a covered procurement/agency request.

questions.question: Confirm which FMLA tracker HR actually edits/relies on in current operations and designate it authoritative. Drive metadata now suggests the native Google Sheet was created as a conversion/derivative of the legacy XLS on May 15, 2026, but timestamps alone do not prove operational authority. Document owner, access controls, backup/retention and integration with Attendance/ADP.
questions.resolution_note: The legacy XLS shows stored modification 2026-05-15 18:17:32Z. The native Google Sheet's first revision is 18:17:58Z with a second revision at 18:18:51Z, consistent with near-immediate conversion/import. No later revision history was observed in either copy. This narrows the duplication question but does not establish which file HR currently treats as authoritative.

questions.question: Validate the remaining Attendance Tracker business-rule assumptions and designate ownership: whether Reserve Hours are the handbook's three additional unpaid attendance days, whether the 24-hour balance resets on hire-date anniversary, which employees legitimately use an 8-hour day assumption, who owns SupervisorBlacklist, and how manual Points tracker entries reconcile to the current six-point/60-day/365-day handbook rules.
questions.resolution_note: Formula-only audit completed without reading employee rows. Attendance has three formulas: ADP normalization/daily aggregation with SupervisorBlacklist exclusion, 8-hours-minus-total shortfall, and a reserve running balance that resets to 24 hours after hire-date anniversary. Points tracker, Blacklist and Previous Months have no formulas in the inspected ranges and are manually maintained state. The current handbook validates the six-point attendance framework and three additional unpaid days, but does not explicitly validate the spreadsheet's 24-hour anniversary reset or universal 8-hour-day assumption.

These software defaults do not themselves prove the approved current HR form/signature/approval chain; local rules/templates and business approval still require validation.
